Comment Management: Functional integration tests for lesson comments (CommentController) and admin moderation (AdminCommentController)
Anyone can view a lesson's approved comment thread without logging in.
column3:
1. Identify a lesson that already has at least one APPROVED comment.
2. Discard any Authorization token.
3. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/comments/lesson/{lessonId}.
4. Inspect the response body's list of comments.
column4: 1. 200 OK; List<CommentDTO> of APPROVED comments (plus the caller's own PENDING ones, if authenticated).
column5: - A lesson with ≥1 APPROVED comment exists.

Comment Management: Posting, editing, or deleting a comment now genuinely requires a valid JWT — regression check for a previously-fixed identity-spoofing gap (there is no longer a client-controlled userId parameter anywhere).
column3:
1. Discard any Authorization token.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/comments/lesson/{lessonId} body {"content":"test"} with no Authorization header.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response status and confirm no comment row was created.
column4: 1. Rejected before reaching the comment logic (401/403 depending on filter-chain behavior — confirm which live) — NOT a 200 success as an old, now-fixed gap once allowed.

Comment Management: A comment with clean, unremarkable text is automatically approved by the moderation rule engine and becomes immediately visible.
column3:
1. Log in as any authenticated role.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/comments/lesson/{lessonId} body {"content":"This lesson was really helpful, thanks!"}.
3. Send the request and inspect the returned status.
4. GET the lesson's thread (per COMMENT_FT01) to confirm the comment is now publicly visible.
column4: 1. 200 OK; the returned CommentDTO has status=APPROVED and is immediately visible to everyone via COMMENT_FT01.
column5: - Logged in (any authenticated role — no role restriction on commenting).

Comment Management: A comment containing a blacklisted profanity keyword is auto-rejected by the rule engine, with the detection reason recorded on the row.
column3:
1. Log in as any authenticated role.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/comments/lesson/{lessonId} with content containing a known blacklisted profanity term.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the returned comment's status and detectionReason.
column4: 1. 200 OK (the POST itself succeeds); the comment's status is REJECTED, with detectionReason "Blacklist keyword detected: "<word>"""""."

Comment Management: A comment containing a mild/suspicious (not blacklisted) keyword is held for review instead of being auto-approved or auto-rejected.
column3:
1. Log in as any authenticated role.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/comments/lesson/{lessonId} with content containing a mild insult keyword (e.g. "ngu", "stupid", "idiot").
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the returned comment's status and detectionReason.

Comment Management: A comment containing a phone number, URL, email, or off-platform-contact phrase is also flagged for review rather than auto-approved.
column3:
1. Log in as any authenticated role.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/comments/lesson/{lessonId} with content containing a Vietnamese phone-number pattern (e.g. "0912345678") or the word "zalo"/"inbox".
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the returned comment's status and detectionReason.
column4: 1. Comment status=PENDING, detectionReason describes the matched pattern (e.g. "Contains a phone number").

Comment Management: A comment held as PENDING is visible only to its own author, and completely absent from another viewer's copy of the same thread.
column3:
1. Post a comment that lands in PENDING (per COMMENT_FT05/06), noting its author.
2. As that same author, GET the lesson's comment thread.
3. Log in as a different user and GET the same lesson's comment thread.
4. Compare both lists for the presence of the PENDING comment.
column4:
1. Step 2: the PENDING comment IS visible to its author.
2. Step 3-4: the SAME comment is absent from a different viewer's list.
column5: - A PENDING comment exists from a known author.

Comment Management: A REJECTED comment is hidden from everyone, including its own original author.
column3:
1. Post a comment that gets auto-REJECTED (per COMMENT_FT04), noting its author.
2. As that same author, GET the lesson's comment thread.
3. Confirm the rejected comment does not appear anywhere in the response.
column4: 1. The rejected comment does NOT appear in the author's own view of the thread either — only visible via the admin moderation endpoints.

Comment Management: Editing a rejected comment's text into something clean automatically re-approves it, with no separate manual resubmission step required.
column3:
1. Have a REJECTED comment (per COMMENT_FT04/08) as its author.
2. Prepare PUT /api/v1/comments/{commentId} body {"content":"This is now a clean, helpful comment."}.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the returned status and confirm it is now visible in the public thread.
column4: 1. 200 OK; the comment's status flips to APPROVED automatically, since the same rule engine re-evaluates on every edit.
column5: - A REJECTED comment owned by the caller.

Comment Management: A user cannot edit or delete another user's comment — but the denial is masked to a generic 500 rather than a clean 403/404.
column3:
1. Log in as User A and post a comment; note its id.
2. Log out and log in as an unrelated User B.
3. Prepare and send PUT /api/v1/comments/{commentIdOwnedByA} body {"content":"hacked"} as User B; inspect the response.
4. Prepare and send DELETE /api/v1/comments/{commentIdOwnedByA} as User B; inspect the response.
column4: 1. Both: 500 Internal Server Error, generic masked body — the real "You are not allowed to edit/delete this comment" RuntimeException is swallowed rather than surfaced as 403.
column5: - A comment owned by User A exists; caller is User B.

Comment Management: Any authenticated user can like an approved comment and then unlike it, with the like count reflecting both actions.
column3:
1. Log in as any authenticated role and identify an APPROVED comment.
2. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/comments/{id}/like; inspect the returned like count.
3. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/comments/{id}/unlike.
4. Inspect the returned like count again to confirm it decremented.
column4: 1. Both: 200 OK, returned CommentDTO reflects the updated like count/state.
column5: - Logged in; an APPROVED comment exists.

Comment Management: HTML/script content submitted in a comment is stored and returned verbatim with no output sanitization (documented, not yet fixed — do not treat as newly discovered).
column3:
1. Log in as any authenticated role.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/comments/lesson/{lessonId} body {"content":"<script>alert(1)</script>"}.
3. Send the request.
4. GET the lesson's thread and inspect the raw JSON response for that comment's content field.
column4: 1. The raw content field contains the literal, unescaped <script> tag — no server-side sanitization/encoding is applied.

Comment Management: Admin views the full moderation queue and a single comment's detail, confirming the detail view exposes extra moderation-only fields hidden from the list.
column3:
1. Log in as ADMINISTRATOR in an environment with comments of multiple statuses.
2. Prepare and send GET /api/admin/comments; inspect the fields present on each list item.
3. Pick one comment's id and prepare/send GET /api/admin/comments/{id}.
4. Compare the detail response's fields against the list response's fields.
column4:
1. Step 2: list of all comments (any status) with id/type/commenter/status/etc, but NOT originalContent/normalizedContent/detectionReason.
2. Step 3-4: same fields PLUS originalContent, normalizedContent, and detectionReason.
column5: - ADMINISTRATOR logged in; comments of multiple statuses exist.

Comment Management: Admin can set a comment's status to any arbitrary string, since there is no whitelist validation on this endpoint.
column3:
1. Log in as ADMINISTRATOR and identify an existing comment's id.
2. Prepare PUT /api/admin/comments/{id}/status?status=garbage.
3. Send the request.
4. GET the comment's admin detail to confirm the persisted status value.
column4: 1. 200 {"success":true,"message":"Comment status updated successfully"}; the comment's status is persisted literally as "GARBAGE" (uppercased) — no enum/whitelist check rejects it.
column5: - ADMINISTRATOR logged in; a comment exists.

Comment Management: Admin can hard-delete a comment, and attempting to operate on a non-existent comment id returns a clean plain-string 404.
column3:
1. Log in as ADMINISTRATOR and identify an existing comment's id.
2. Prepare and send DELETE /api/admin/comments/{that id}; confirm it disappears from the moderation queue.
3. Prepare DELETE /api/admin/comments/999999 (an id confirmed not to exist).
4. Inspect the response status and body shape.
column4: 1. 404, plain-text body "Comment not found" (not JSON) — note this specific shape when asserting the response.
